calls.video_title: I'll Buy or Sell SoFi After Earnings. Here's What Decides It
calls.stance_flip: Couch Investor was HOLD on SOFI (most recent tracked call, 9 Oct backfill entry), now CONDITIONAL_BUY — will buy more after earnings only if the report is strong and management gives assurance on its targets; explicitly not selling
calls.price_at_call: trading under $15 (stated); down ~50% over 12 months, ~55% drawdown from peak; market cap $18.6bn (stated); P/E 30x, forward 20x, PEG 0.5 (stated); his DCF bull $28 / base $22.80 / bear $10, ~51.3% upside on his assumptions
calls.thesis: CONDITIONAL_BUY — he will buy more SoFi shares next week if Q3 (Tue 27 Oct, pre-market) is an extremely good report and management assures shareholders it can still meet its own mid-term targets in a harsher rate environment; as of now he is waiting, and he is definitely not selling.
calls.base_case: His Q3 predictions: revenue $1.28bn (consensus ~$1.25bn), adjusted EBITDA $435m at a 34% margin (on track for the $1.6bn target), diluted EPS $0.17, over 1m new members at ~$322 acquisition cost; financial services ~$500m, lending ~$745m at a 56% contribution margin, Galileo ~$90m sequential growth; FY26 EPS guidance $0.60.
calls.bull_case: Bull DCF case $28/share (30% probability in his model): SoFi keeps beating consensus as it has in recent quarters (revenue beats of 7.1%, 3.6%, 3.1%; EPS beats of ~10%+) and management confirms the 30% growth compounding for the next ~2.5 years.
calls.bear_case: Bear DCF case $10/share (20% probability): management cannot deliver its targets, especially if the high-rate environment worsens into 2027; the stock was arguably too expensive near $30 at the start of the year, which he concedes may explain part of the 50% fall.

calls.video_title: Should You Buy SoFi Stock Before the Huge Investor Update?
calls.thesis: CONDITIONAL_BUY (soft flip from BUY on 2026-10-15; long-term stance unchanged) — long-term buying opportunity / bullish, fair value raised $19 to $19.82 vs $14.82 market (~34% upside over 12-18 months, forward P/E 18.5), but do NOT buy before the Tue 27 Oct investor update: he sees very little upside into the print as macro/rate headwinds have worsened, and personally would wait until after it to decide. Optional FOMO route he personally would not use: 25% before / 75% after.
calls.base_case: Most recent quarter (reported 29 Jul): revenue +43% to $1.2bn, adjusted EBITDA +44%, members +35% YoY to 15.8m (+1.1m in the quarter), loan originations $14.8bn; digital-only model lets SoFi invest in products over legacy branch costs.
calls.bull_case: If the technology platform reinvigorates growth after losing a large client (accounts -16% YoY to 135m, +2m QoQ), SoFi can earn a technology valuation rather than a muted bank valuation.
calls.bear_case: Higher and faster-rising rates likely cut the fair value of the $46.6bn loan book (at 30 Jun) by several billions and lower loan-sale prices; oil/inflation/macro headwinds worsened in the quarter to be reported 27 Oct, and the tech segment continues to struggle to add customers.

calls.video_title: Why Is SoFi Stock Crashing, and is it a Generational Buying Opportunity?
calls.thesis: First tracked Parkevtate SOFI call — BUY / 'buying opportunity' (he upgraded at ~$18 earlier). Stock down 12% in a month, -46% YTD on higher rates; forward P/E 18.5; sees >24% upside over 12-18 months to his $19 fair value. Above-average risk.
calls.base_case: Lending segment booming (Q2 segment revenue +63% YoY) with strong third-party loan demand.
calls.bear_case: Higher rates cut the fair value of its $46.6bn loan book (likely billions), default rates rising (personal loans 4.57%->4.77% Mar-Jun) and likely up again; consumer/macro headwinds worsening.
